description: Yale-Brown Obsessive Compulsive Scale (Y-BOCS) - Standard 10-question version. Measures severity of obsessions and compulsions. Each question scored 0-4. Total score range 0-40.
name: Y-BOCS Standard

questions.option_1: Less than 1 hr/day or occasional occurrence
questions.option_3: Greater than 3 and up to 8 hrs/day or very frequent occurrence
questions.option_4: Greater than 8 hrs/day or nearly constant occurrence
questions.question: 1. TIME OCCUPIED BY OBSESSIVE THOUGHTS - How much of your time is occupied by obsessive thoughts?

questions.option_1: Slight interference with social or other activities, but overall performance not impaired
questions.option_2: Definite interference with social or occupational performance, but still manageable
questions.option_3: Causes substantial impairment in social or occupational performance
questions.question: 2. INTERFERENCE DUE TO OBSESSIVE THOUGHTS - How much do your obsessive thoughts interfere with your work, school, social, or other important role functioning?
3. DISTRESS ASSOCIATED WITH OBSESSIVE THOUGHTS - How much distress do your obsessive thoughts cause you?

questions.option_0: Try to resist all the time
questions.option_1: Try to resist most of the time
questions.option_3: Yield to all obsessions without attempting to control them, but with some reluctance
questions.option_4: Completely and willingly yield to all obsessions
questions.question: 4. RESISTANCE AGAINST OBSESSIONS - How much effort do you make to resist the obsessive thoughts?

questions.option_1: Usually able to stop or divert obsessions with some effort and concentration
questions.option_2: Sometimes able to stop or divert obsessions
questions.option_3: Rarely successful in stopping or dismissing obsessions, can only divert attention with difficulty
questions.option_4: Obsessions are completely involuntary, rarely able to even momentarily alter obsessive thinking
questions.question: 5. DEGREE OF CONTROL OVER OBSESSIVE THOUGHTS - How much control do you have over your obsessive thoughts?

questions.option_1: Less than 1 hr/day or occasional performance of compulsive behaviors
questions.option_2: 1 to 3 hrs/day or frequent performance of compulsive behaviors
questions.option_3: More than 3 and up to 8 hrs/day or very frequent performance of compulsive behaviors
questions.option_4: More than 8 hrs/day or near constant performance of compulsive behaviors
questions.question: 6. TIME SPENT PERFORMING COMPULSIVE BEHAVIORS - How much time do you spend performing compulsive behaviors?

questions.option_1: Slight interference with social or other activities, but overall performance not impaired
questions.option_2: Definite interference with social or occupational performance, but still manageable
questions.option_3: Causes substantial impairment in social or occupational performance
questions.question: 7. INTERFERENCE DUE TO COMPULSIVE BEHAVIORS - How much do your compulsive behaviors interfere with your work, school, social, or other important role functioning?

questions.option_1: Only slightly anxious if compulsions prevented
questions.option_2: Anxiety would mount but remain manageable if compulsions prevented
questions.option_3: Prominent and very disturbing increase in anxiety if compulsions interrupted
questions.option_4: Incapacitating anxiety from any intervention aimed at modifying activity
questions.question: 8. DISTRESS ASSOCIATED WITH COMPULSIVE BEHAVIOR - How would you feel if prevented from performing your compulsion(s)?

questions.option_1: Try to resist most of the time
questions.option_3: Yield to almost all compulsions without attempting to control them, but with some reluctance
questions.option_4: Completely and willingly yield to all compulsions
questions.question: 9. RESISTANCE AGAINST COMPULSIONS - How much effort do you make to resist the compulsions?

questions.option_1: Pressure to perform the behavior but usually able to exercise voluntary control
questions.option_2: Strong pressure to perform behavior, can control it only with difficulty
questions.option_3: Very strong drive to perform behavior, must be carried to completion, can only delay with difficulty
questions.option_4: Drive to perform behavior experienced as completely involuntary and overpowering, rarely able to even momentarily delay activity
questions.question: 10. DEGREE OF CONTROL OVER COMPULSIVE BEHAVIOR - How strong is the drive to perform the compulsive behavior?
